title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 422
paragraphs: After they had seen everything, the spies departed to go back; and when they reported these things, Cambyses was enraged at once and proceeded to march his army against the Ethiopians, not having ordered any provision of food nor even considered that he was proposing to march an army to the furthest ends of the earth. But, like one who is mad and not in his right senses, when he heard the report of the Ichthyophagoi he began the march, ordering those of the Greeks present to remain behind in Egypt, and taking with him the whole of his land force. When in the course of his march he had reached Thebes, he detached about fifty thousand of his army and ordered them to enslave the Ammonians and set fire to the seat of the oracle of Zeus, while he himself with the rest of his army went on against the Ethiopians. But before the army had covered a fifth of the way, all the provisions they had completely ran out; and then, after the provisions, the beasts of burden too were eaten up and were gone. Now if Cambyses, perceiving this, had changed his plan and led his army back, he would have been a wise man despite his first mistake; as it was, however, he paid no regard but went forward without stopping. The soldiers, therefore, as long as they could get anything from the ground, prolonged their lives by eating grass. But when they came to the sand, some did a fearful deed — out of each company of ten they selected one by lot and devoured him. When Cambyses heard this and was alarmed at their eating of one another, he gave up the expedition against the Ethiopians and set out to go back again, and arrived at Thebes having lost a great number of his army. Then from Thebes he came down to Memphis and allowed the Greeks to sail home.
